# Patches

Every patch and game setting FramePort knows: 169 entries in 5 groups. A game's recipe is its chosen patches and settings; tested games get theirs from the catalog ([GAMES.md](GAMES.md)), and other games get the patches FramePort suggests from its analysis. You change them on the game page under Customize.

Each entry says what the patch does, whether it changes the APK or only the install, when FramePort suggests it, its options, the catalog games whose recipe names it and the launch-test signatures that suggest it. Patches that are on by default are on for every game, so the catalog rarely names them.

Link to an entry with its id, dots replaced by dashes: `PATCHES.md#frame-unity_text_input` for `frame.unity_text_input`.

## Groups

- [Patches from OVRPort](#group-overport) (25)
- [Steam Frame patches](#group-frame) (55)
- [Game settings](#group-adapter) (68)

## <a id="group-overport"></a>Patches from OVRPort

OVRPort converts a Quest game's Meta VR code to standard OpenXR; FramePort picks which of its patches run. The list comes from the OVRPort CLI at runtime (new OVRPort patches appear in the app on their own); this page shows FramePort's bundled list (`patches/overport.py`).

### <a id="patch_ac_nexus_no_appsw_72"></a>AC Nexus: no AppSW at 72 Hz

Assassin's Creed Nexus: smoother picture at 72 Hz (turns off Meta's frame-rate trick).

- `patch_ac_nexus_no_appsw_72`
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (during the OVRPort conversion).
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Only for its game's build:** outside it the whole OVRPort run fails, so recipes only use it where it applies.
- **Conflicts with:** [`patch_ac_nexus_no_appsw_90`](#patch_ac_nexus_no_appsw_90)
- **Source:** [patches/overport.py](../src/frameport/patches/overport.py)

> Assassin's Creed Nexus (build 207706 only): turns off application space warp and runs at 72 Hz.

### <a id="patch_ac_nexus_no_appsw_90"></a>AC Nexus: no AppSW at 90 Hz

Assassin's Creed Nexus: smoother picture at 90 Hz (turns off Meta's frame-rate trick).

- `patch_ac_nexus_no_appsw_90`
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (during the OVRPort conversion).
- **Suggested (on):** This Assassin's Creed Nexus build runs smoothly on the Frame without application space warp, at 90 Hz.
- **Only for its game's build:** outside it the whole OVRPort run fails, so recipes only use it where it applies.
- **Conflicts with:** [`patch_ac_nexus_no_appsw_72`](#patch_ac_nexus_no_appsw_72)
- **Catalog games (1):** Assassin's Creed Nexus.
- **Source:** [patches/overport.py](../src/frameport/patches/overport.py)

> Assassin's Creed Nexus (build 207706 only): turns off application space warp and runs at 90 Hz.

### <a id="patch_clean_up_frida"></a>Clean up Frida leftovers in smali

Removes debugging leftovers some game files contain.

- `patch_clean_up_frida` · on by default
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (during the OVRPort conversion).
- **Suggested (on):** Part of every OVRPort conversion.
- **Source:** [patches/overport.py](../src/frameport/patches/overport.py)

> Removes leftovers from dumped/modded APKs.

### <a id="patch_copy_libraries"></a>Copy OVRPort libraries

Adds the parts that let a Quest game run on the Steam Frame. Needed for every Quest game.

- `patch_copy_libraries` · on by default
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (during the OVRPort conversion).
- **Suggested (on):** Part of every OVRPort conversion.
- **Source:** [patches/overport.py](../src/frameport/patches/overport.py)

> Adds OVRPort's OpenXR loader dispatcher and platform loader. Required: without it nothing is translated.

### <a id="patch_copy_ovrplugin_vrapi"></a>Copy OVRPlugin if VrApi is present

Gives older Quest games a newer version of Meta's VR plugin that can be converted.

- `patch_copy_ovrplugin_vrapi` · on by default
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (during the OVRPort conversion).
- **Suggested (on):** Part of every OVRPort conversion.
- **Source:** [patches/overport.py](../src/frameport/patches/overport.py)

> Swaps in an OpenXR OVRPlugin for games that use VrApi through OVRPlugin (older Unity/Unreal).

### <a id="patch_disable_controller_offset"></a>Disable controller tracking offset

Removes a controller position adjustment, for games whose hands look misplaced.

- `patch_disable_controller_offset`
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (during the OVRPort conversion).
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Source:** [patches/overport.py](../src/frameport/patches/overport.py)

> Removes OVRPort's controller pose offset if controllers look misplaced.

### <a id="patch_disable_meta_xr_audio_telemetry"></a>Disable Meta XR Audio telemetry

Stops Meta's audio library from reporting to Meta (only matters on PC emulators).

- `patch_disable_meta_xr_audio_telemetry`
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (during the OVRPort conversion).
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Source:** [patches/overport.py](../src/frameport/patches/overport.py)

> Skips Meta XR Audio's telemetry under x86_64 ARM translation (emulators). Not needed on the Frame, which runs games natively.

### <a id="patch_disable_space_warp"></a>Disable application space warp if used

Turns off Meta's frame-rate trick, which causes glitches or hangs outside Quest headsets.

- `patch_disable_space_warp`
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (during the OVRPort conversion).

## <a id="group-frame"></a>Steam Frame patches

FramePort's own changes to a converted Quest game, for what the Steam Frame lacks or does differently.

### <a id="frame-a32_bridge"></a>32-bit ARM bridge (Gear VR / Go games)

Runs a 32-bit game (Gear VR, Oculus Go, early Quest) on the Frame, which only runs 64-bit code. Experimental.

- `frame.a32_bridge` · experimental · also for 2D apps
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested (on):** 32-bit-only game: the Frame can't run 32-bit ARM code, the bridge translates it.
- **Catalog games (6):** AFFECTED: The Manor, Gunjack, Journey of the Gods, Shadow Point, Sports Scramble (Santa Cruz), Spunky Dungeon.
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `no-arm64` (fatal): 32-bit-only APK (e.g. a Gear VR or Oculus Go game).
- **Source:** [patches/frame/a32_bridge.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/a32_bridge.py)

> Runs a 32-bit-only game (armeabi-v7a: Gear VR, Oculus Go and early Quest games) on the Frame, which has no 32-bit ARM support: an AArch32 → AArch64 translator inside the app runs the game's own libraries, with GLES/EGL, OpenSL ES and VrApi translated to the Frame's 64-bit ones (VrApi through the VrApi → OpenXR bridge). The Gear VR / Go controller: left stick = touchpad (walk, strafe), right stick sideways = turn (a click at the touchpad's edge), stick press or A = click, right trigger, B = back. Experimental: games run slower than native ones.

### <a id="frame-adapter"></a>FrameBridge OpenXR adapter

FramePort's layer between the game and the Steam Frame: fills in what the Frame lacks (controllers, room, passthrough). Needed for every converted game.

- `frame.adapter` · on by default
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested (on):** Required for every OpenXR/overport build on the Frame.
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `cube-swapchain-refused` (fatal): The game asked for a cube-map swapchain (for example an OVROverlay skybox or loading cube), which the Frame's runtime doesn't have.
  - `cylinder-menu-layers-rejected` (error): The game draws a curved (cylinder) screen to each eye separately (for example the Doom3Quest / PreyVR menu).
  - `graphics-requirements-missing` (fatal): The game can't start VR on the Frame; rebuild it with the current FramePort.
  - `swapchain-rect-invalid` (fatal): The runtime rejects the game's frames, so it stops drawing (for example stuck at a "Waiting" box).
  - `time-conversion` (warning): The Frame's runtime lacks timespec time conversion; the current adapter build emulates it.
- **Source:** [patches/frame/adapter.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/adapter.py)

> Wraps OVRPort's generic OpenXR loader (renamed libopenxr_loader_original.so). Fixes the Frame runtime's gaps: retries rejected GLES swapchain formats/MSAA (Frame takes sRGB only), drops unsupported instance extensions and layers, emulates XR_FB_passthrough (ALPHA_BLEND), Meta scene/spatial entities (guardian-sized room), XR_KHR_convert_timespec_time, and vertically flipped quad layers; maps Frame controllers to Touch; optionally serves Steam Frame controller models (XR_FB_render_model). Its settings are under Game settings.

### <a id="frame-asset_files"></a>Content files from the game's data

Lets the game find extra content it keeps next to its data (for example Star Wars Tales' seasons).

- `frame.asset_files`
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested (on):** The game asks Meta's platform for asset files and its data has … content file(s) (*.pak) that OVRPort's loader doesn't report.
- **Catalog games (2):** Attack on Titan VR: Unbreakable, Star Wars: Tales from the Galaxy's Edge.
- **Source:** [patches/frame/langpack.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/langpack.py)

> Some games keep content in separate files next to their OBB (for example Star Wars: Tales from the Galaxy's Edge: its seasons and sound banks) and ask Meta's platform for them as asset files. OVRPort's platform loader doesn't know them, so the game waits for content that never arrives (black screen after loading). Lists the content files shipped with the game's data (*.pak) as installed and answers their download request at once with the file's path; nothing is copied or downloaded. Shares the language-pack library.

- `frame.asset_files_stub` · experimental

- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `meta-asset-status-error` (error): A DLC manager reports a Meta asset-file status error after VR starts (e.g.
- **Source:** [patches/frame/langpack.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/langpack.py)

> Experimental bypass for a DLC manager blocked on Meta asset-file service errors at startup (e.g. PixelRipped 1995: Asset status error (code 100)). Returns an empty successful asset list and reports requested asset IDs as installed, with an empty file path. Does not supply DLC or change download requests. Enable only to test this startup failure; disable with FRAMEPORT_ASSET_FILES_STUB=0. Shares the language-pack library and needs no language packs.

- **Catalog games (1):** BlazeRush.

Stops bHaptics from asking for a Bluetooth permission the Frame doesn't have (the game would freeze on its loading screen).

- `frame.bhaptics_permission` · also for 2D apps
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).

- **Catalog games (5):** Quantum Void, Ragnarock, Smash Drums, Tea For God, Vendetta Forever.

- **Source:** [patches/frame/bhaptics_permission.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/bhaptics_permission.py)

The request returns at once instead (an in-place edit of classes.dex).

### <a id="frame-blazerush"></a>BlazeRush: controllers without Meta avatars, own shader cache

Makes BlazeRush's menus and controllers work without Meta's avatars, and lets its shader fixes take effect.

- `frame.blazerush`
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Only for its game's build:** outside it the whole OVRPort run fails, so recipes only use it where it applies.
- **Catalog games (1):** BlazeRush.
- **Source:** [patches/frame/blazerush.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/blazerush.py)

> BlazeRush 1.0.349 only (Klownicle's guide, GitHub #57). Its menus wait for Meta's avatar, which never comes on the Frame, before they create the game's own controllers: the second menu ignored all input. Two instructions in libtargemapp.so skip that wait and the avatar mesh drawing; the game's shader cache gets a new folder name (cache/br_shader_v1), so programs compiled before the GL shim's shader fixes aren't reused. Only this exact build is changed (code fingerprint and every instruction checked); anything else is left as it is.

### <a id="frame-eos_keychain_loop"></a>Epic Online Services: stop the keychain retry loop

Stops Epic Online Services from retrying its login keychain forever (the game would never finish starting).

- `frame.eos_keychain_loop` · also for 2D apps
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `eos-keychain-loop` (error): Epic Online Services can't save its login keychain and retries without end (a start that never finishes, 100 % CPU).
- **Source:** [patches/frame/eos_keychain_loop.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/eos_keychain_loop.py)

> Epic Online Services (EOS) keeps its login keychain in the app's settings storage. When it can't write there, it resets the keychain and tries again without end (for example Beyond Sandbox: a start that never finishes, 100 % CPU, a log of gigabytes). The reset method returns at once instead (an in-place edit of classes.dex), so EOS reports the failure to the game once.

### <a id="frame-gl_multiview_fbo"></a>OpenGL ES: multiview shaders on flat panels (HUD, menus)

Experimental: shows HUDs, menus and other flat panels that stay black on the Frame (for example Doom3Quest's HUD and PDA).

- `frame.gl_multiview_fbo` · experimental
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Offered (off):** Own OpenGL ES engine with multiview shaders: turn on if HUD, menu or other flat panels stay black on the Frame (for example Doom3Quest's HUD and PDA).
- **Catalog games (1):** Doom3Quest.
- **Source:** [patches/frame/gl_multiview_fbo.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/gl_multiview_fbo.py)

> Some OpenGL ES engines compile every shader for multiview (both eyes in one draw, `num_views=2`) and use the same shaders to draw into ordinary single-layer framebuffers, for example a HUD or PDA screen rendered to a texture. Quest's driver draws them anyway; the Frame's driver (Mesa) follows the OVR_multiview rule and silently drops every such draw, so those panels stay black (for example Doom3Quest's HUD and PDA). Loads OpenGL ES through a small interposer (libfpglmv.so) that draws those cases with a single-view copy of the shader program (left-eye view; uniforms copied before each such draw). Eye-buffer draws are unchanged. Logs under the tag GLMV; the setting gl_mv_debug adds error checks and counters.

### <a id="frame-gl_shim"></a>GL shim (Mesa GLSL compatibility)

Corrects graphics code the Frame's drivers reject (black screen with sound).

- `frame.gl_shim` · experimental
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested (on):** GLES engine resolving GL through eglGetProcAddress (GLAD) on the VrApi bridge.
- **Requires:** [`frame.vrapi_bridge`](#frame-vrapi_bridge)
- **Catalog games (2):** BlazeRush, Path of the Warrior.
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `gl-shader-failed` (error): The game's shaders don't compile on the Frame, so parts of the picture are missing.
- **Source:** [patches/frame/vrapi_bridge.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/vrapi_bridge.py)

> Loads libglshim.so ahead of libEGL in every engine library that fetches GL through eglGetProcAddress. Fixes Quest-only leniency that Mesa/Zink rejects: #pragma before #extension, implicit int/float conversions (enables GL_EXT_shader_implicit_conversions), and multiview shaders used on single-view framebuffers (hides GL_OVR_multiview; gl_hide_multiview=0 turns that off). Logs every failed shader with its source lines (logcat tag GLShim). Symptom: black screen with working audio in a GLES game.

### <a id="frame-godot_clipboard"></a>Godot apps: start without a clipboard service

Lets Godot games start on the Frame (they'd crash looking for a clipboard).

- `frame.godot_clipboard` · also for 2D apps
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested (on):** Godot 4 app: it crashes at start in Lepton, which has no clipboard service.
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `godot-no-clipboard` (fatal): The app crashed at start because the Frame's Android has no clipboard.
- **Source:** [patches/frame/godot_clipboard.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/godot_clipboard.py)

> Lepton's Android has no clipboard service, and the Android code of Godot 4.2-4.4 (for example EndoparasiticVR) casts the missing service to a ClipboardManager without checking, so the app crashes at start with a NullPointerException in Godot.&lt;init&gt;. That check is skipped and Godot's clipboard functions do nothing instead (an in-place edit of classes.dex).

### <a id="frame-hw_video_decode"></a>Hardware video decoding (H.264, HEVC, VP9)

Plays the game's videos on the Frame's video hardware, so 4K and 8K video runs smoothly.

- `frame.hw_video_decode` · also for 2D apps
- **Changes:** Install only: written on the Frame when the game is installed; the APK isn't changed.
- **Suggested (on):** The game plays video through Android's decoders (MediaCodec, ExoPlayer or VLC): decode it on the Frame's hardware.
- **Catalog games (23):** 4XVR Video Player, AugmentedEmpire, Batman: Arkham Shadow, Battlemarked, Breathedge VR, Dance Central, Exploding Kittens VR, Eye of the Temple and 15 more.
- **Source:** [patches/frame/hw_video_decode.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/hw_video_decode.py)

> Decodes the game's videos on the Frame's hardware video decoder instead of Android's software decoders, which stutter or fall behind with 4K/8K video (for example video players, Batman: Arkham Shadow's cutscenes). Adds FramePort's codec plugin (OMX.frameport.avc/hevc/vp9.decoder) to this game's container only; the APK isn't changed. When the hardware is busy (for example Steam's own hardware video decoding is on) the video is decoded in software as before.

### <a id="frame-langpacks"></a>Language packs from the game's files

Lets the game use language files already in its data instead of waiting for a download that never comes.

- `frame.langpacks` · experimental
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Source:** [patches/frame/langpack.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/langpack.py)

> OVRPort's platform loader answers the Meta Platform SDK's language-pack calls (ovr_LanguagePack_GetCurrent/SetCurrent) with 'no request', so a game that asks for its language pack never gets an answer. Adds a small library that serves language packs (&lt;tag&gt;.lang, for example de.lang) found in the game's own data folders (OBB and app files) through the same calls, the asset-file list and the status call, without any download. The game then finds the file path itself. The pack it applies with SetCurrent wins; otherwise the environment variable FRAMEPORT_LANGPACK (a tag), otherwise the only pack there is. Everything else goes to the loader unchanged. Off by default: turn it on for a game whose data has such files (the game page lists the patch only then).

### <a id="frame-launcher"></a>Launcher category (INFO → LAUNCHER)

Makes the game start from the Frame's Steam library.

- `frame.launcher` · on by default · also for 2D apps
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested (on):** Manifest uses category INFO only; Lepton needs LAUNCHER.
- **Suggested (on):** Applied automatically if the manifest needs it.
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `no-launcher` (fatal): Nothing starts: Lepton found no entry point in the app (an activity with category LAUNCHER).
- **Source:** [patches/frame/manifest_fixes.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/manifest_fixes.py)

> Lepton only launches an activity with category LAUNCHER (Quest apps often use INFO). Symptom when missing: launch.log says 'APP_ACTIVITY is empty' and nothing starts.

### <a id="frame-ltw_depth"></a>GL wrapper: OpenGL ES depth formats (Minecraft)

Stops a black picture in Minecraft launchers (for example QuestCraft).

- `frame.ltw_depth` · on by default · also for 2D apps
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested (on):** Ships LTW (Minecraft's OpenGL-to-OpenGL ES wrapper): Minecraft's 32-bit depth textures need the OpenGL ES format on the Frame (for example QuestCraft).
- **Source:** [patches/frame/ltw_depth.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/ltw_depth.py)

> Minecraft asks for desktop OpenGL's GL_DEPTH_COMPONENT32 depth textures. Some builds of LTW, the OpenGL-to-OpenGL ES wrapper in Minecraft launchers such as QuestCraft, pass that on unchanged; Quest's driver accepts it, the Frame's Mesa rejects it (GL_INVALID_OPERATION in glTexImage2D), so the depth buffer never exists and the picture stays black. LTW then loads OpenGL ES through a small shim that asks for GL_DEPTH_COMPONENT32F (or 24-bit) instead.

### <a id="frame-luajit_pointers"></a>Fix Lua startup crashes on Frame

Lets games with a verified older Lua engine get past a startup crash on the Frame.

- `frame.luajit_pointers`
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested (on):** The bundled Lua engine rejects Frame's wider native pointers; use the compatible full-pointer engine while retaining the game's bindings.
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `lua-lightuserdata-pointer` (fatal): The Lua runtime rejected a pointer outside its supported address range.
- **Source:** [patches/frame/luajit_pointers.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/luajit_pointers.py)

> Older xLua/LuaJIT engines reject native pointers outside their 47-bit range, causing a startup error and sometimes a second crash during Unity shutdown (e.g. BattleTalent). Uses a Lua engine that preserves full pointer values while keeping the game's original xLua bindings and native helpers. Applied only to the verified compatible library build.

### <a id="frame-meta_permissions"></a>Declare Meta-only permissions

Declares Meta's permissions some mixed-reality games ask for, so they don't stop.

- `frame.meta_permissions`
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).

- **Catalog games (3):** Arkio, Demeter, Real VR Fishing.
- **Source:** [patches/frame/manifest_fixes.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/manifest_fixes.py)

### <a id="frame-metaxr_telemetry"></a>Meta XR Audio: skip Quest telemetry class

Skips a Quest-only reporting step in Meta's audio library that crashes some games.

- `frame.metaxr_telemetry` · on by default
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested (on):** Meta XR Audio present; patched automatically if it has the telemetry lookup.
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `oculus-os-class` (fatal): The game looks up a Quest-only system class and aborts.
- **Source:** [patches/frame/telemetry.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/telemetry.py)

### <a id="frame-nodebug"></a>Clear android:debuggable

Stops strict debugging checks that make some games quit.

- `frame.nodebug` · also for 2D apps
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested (on):** Unreal Engine ….…: older UE4 makes JNI calls CheckJNI rejects (for example Time Stall aborted on GetStringUTFChars(NULL)).
- **Suggested (on):** Unreal build of Meta XR Audio: its telemetry lookup leaves a pending JNI exception that CheckJNI turns into an abort (for example NOPE Challenge).
- **Offered (off):** Enable if the game aborts with 'JNI DETECTED ERROR' (CheckJNI).
- **Catalog games (3):** ExploreVR, NOPE CHALLENGE, Time Stall.
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**

- **Source:** [patches/frame/manifest_fixes.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/manifest_fixes.py)

Provides stand-ins for Quest system calls some games make at start.

- `frame.oculusos`

- **Suggested (on):** The Unreal build of Meta XR Audio looks up com.oculus.os.AnalyticsEvent and aborts without it (for example NOPE Challenge).
- **Suggested (on):** Several Meta SDK libraries look up com.oculus.os.AnalyticsEvent (…); games like this abort without the stub (for example Nano).
- **Offered (off):** … references com.oculus.os.AnalyticsEvent; usually harmless (for example Batman: Arkham Shadow and LEGO Bricktales run without it). Enable if the game aborts with ClassNotFoundException.
- **Catalog games (17):** AgeOfJoy, AllInOneSports, Caves, Deep Cuts, Does it Stack?, Nano, Neko Atsume Purrfect, NOPE CHALLENGE and 9 more.

### <a id="frame-ovr_microphone"></a>Fix crash when the game prepares the microphone

Stops a crash a few seconds after the logo in games with voice chat.

- `frame.ovr_microphone`
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested (on):** The game uses Meta's microphone API (ovr_Microphone_GetOutputBufferMaxSize), which crashes in OVRPort's library before the microphone is started.
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `ovr-microphone-crash` (fatal): The game crashed while setting up the microphone (for example Unreal's Oculus voice chat a few seconds after the logo).
- **Source:** [patches/frame/ovr_microphone.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/ovr_microphone.py)

> OVRPort's Meta platform library opens the microphone only when it's started, but answers a game's question about the microphone buffer size from that not-yet-opened stream: games that ask first (Unreal's Oculus voice chat, for example The Walking Dead: Saints & Sinners Ch. 2) crash a few seconds after the logo (SIGSEGV in libaaudio.so). Adds the missing check (size 0 until the microphone is started).

### <a id="frame-ovr_stable_user"></a>Keep the same Meta user between starts

Keeps your progress in games that file their saves under your Meta user.

- `frame.ovr_stable_user` · on by default
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested (on):** The game uses Meta's platform library: OVRPort's version gives it a new user id at every start, which loses saves filed under that id.
- **Source:** [patches/frame/ovr_stable_user.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/ovr_stable_user.py)

> Without a Meta account, OVRPort's platform library makes up a new user id at every start (ovr_GetLoggedInUserID). Games that file saves under the user id (for example Walkabout Mini Golf) then start with an empty profile each time and seem to lose all progress. Gives the game a fixed id instead, different for each game and each FramePort user.

### <a id="frame-ovr_trace"></a>Trace Meta platform requests (diagnostics)

For troubleshooting: records the game's requests to Meta's online services.

- `frame.ovr_trace` · experimental · also for 2D apps
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Source:** [patches/frame/ovr_trace.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/ovr_trace.py)

> Logs every Meta Platform SDK request the game makes (user, entitlement, cloud saves, ...) and the messages that answer them, and every 10 s the requests that never got an answer (logcat tag fp_ovrtrace, in launch.log). For games that wait forever on a loading screen (for example Vader Immortal after its intro). Changes nothing: every call goes to the real function.

### <a id="frame-ovrplatformcompat"></a>Platform compat (ovrMessageType_ToString)

Adds a small piece of Meta's platform library that some games need to start.

- `frame.ovrplatformcompat` · on by default
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested (on):** Applied automatically when the OVRPort build needs it.
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `missing-ovr-symbol` (fatal): The game can't load because OVRPort's platform loader lacks Meta platform functions it uses.
- **Source:** [patches/frame/platform_libs.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/platform_libs.py)

> Adds a real ovrMessageType_ToString (OVRPort's platform compat library) for games whose platform loader lacks it (for example The Climb 2). OVRPort 1.2.5+ adds the same library itself; then this is skipped.

### <a id="frame-ovrstubs"></a>Stub missing Meta platform functions

Provides stand-ins for Meta store functions the game expects, so it doesn't crash at start.

- `frame.ovrstubs` · on by default
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested (on):** Applied automatically when the OVRPort build needs it.
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `missing-ovr-symbol` (fatal): The game can't load because OVRPort's platform loader lacks Meta platform functions it uses.
- **Source:** [patches/frame/platform_libs.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/platform_libs.py)

> Generates no-op stubs for ovr_* functions the game imports but OVRPort's platform loader lacks (for example Espire 1/2, Wallace & Gromit, The Climb 2). Symptom: UnsatisfiedLinkError / 'cannot locate symbol ovr_...'. Online/store features stay unavailable.

### <a id="frame-pac_hints"></a>Unpaired pointer-authentication checks

Stops a crash on the Frame's processor in games whose code the Quest runs more leniently (for example Star Wars Pinball VR).

- `frame.pac_hints`
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Catalog games (1):** Star Wars Pinball VR.
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `pac-unpaired` (fatal): The game crashed on a CPU check the Quest ignores but the Frame enforces.
- **Source:** [patches/frame/pac_hints.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/pac_hints.py)

> Some engines contain assembly (for example OpenSSL's) that checks a return-address signature it never made. The Quest's CPU ignores those checks, the Steam Frame's enforces them: the game crashes with SIGILL as soon as it uses that code, for example on its first network connection (Star Wars Pinball VR). In a library with unpaired checks, the signing and checking instructions become no-ops.

### <a id="frame-sdl_clipboard"></a>SDL apps: start without a clipboard service

Lets SDL and LÖVE games start on the Frame (they'd crash looking for a clipboard).

- `frame.sdl_clipboard` · also for 2D apps
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested (on):** SDL app: it crashes at start in Lepton, which has no clipboard service.
- **Catalog games (5):** Crisis Zone VR, Majora's Mask VR, Time Crisis II VR (Test), Time Crisis VR (Experimental), WiiCompiled VR.
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `sdl-no-clipboard` (fatal): The app crashed at start because the Frame's Android has no clipboard.
- **Source:** [patches/frame/sdl_clipboard.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/sdl_clipboard.py)

> Lepton's Android has no clipboard service, and SDL's Java code (SDL2 and LÖVE games, for example Dramatic Shape) registers a clipboard listener at start without checking, so the app crashes with a NullPointerException in SDLClipboardHandler. That call is skipped (an in-place edit of classes.dex).

### <a id="frame-slz_vulkan_hooks"></a>Stress Level Zero: let Unity start Vulkan itself

Stops a start-up crash in Stress Level Zero games (for example BONELAB).

- `frame.slz_vulkan_hooks`
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested (on):** Stress Level Zero's graphics plugin crashes Unity's Vulkan start-up on the Frame (for example BONELAB 1.2974).
- **Catalog games (1):** BONELAB.
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `slz-vulkan-hook-crash` (fatal): The game's own graphics plugin crashes or hangs it before the first frame (for example BONELAB 1.2974).
- **Source:** [patches/frame/slz_vulkan_hooks.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/slz_vulkan_hooks.py)

> Stress Level Zero's graphics plugin (libSLZQuestNative.so, for example BONELAB 1.2974) hooks Unity's Vulkan start-up and its texture samplers. On the Frame the hook calls an invalid function while Vulkan starts, and the game crashes or hangs before the first frame. The plugin's two hooks are switched off, so Unity starts Vulkan itself. Its pipeline cache isn't used: the first start spends about half a minute prewarming shaders.

### <a id="frame-start_activity"></a>Start straight in VR (skip the 2D launcher)

Opens the app straight in VR, skipping its flat launcher screen. Turn off to use the launcher, for example to import new content.

- `frame.start_activity` · also for 2D apps
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Offered (off):** The app opens a 2D launcher; its VR part is …. Turn on to start that directly once the app is set up.
- **Options:** `activity`: str, default empty — Activity to start (empty: the app's VR activity)
- **Source:** [patches/frame/manifest_fixes.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/manifest_fixes.py)

> Some apps open a flat Android launcher that then starts a separate VR activity (for example WiiCompiled). Shown with Lepton's flat window, that window stays in view after the VR part starts. This makes the VR activity the one Lepton starts (its LAUNCHER category), so the app opens in VR with no flat window. Everything only the launcher does (choosing or importing content) is skipped: turn it off for a run when you need the launcher, and turn off "Show the app's Android window".

### <a id="frame-swapchain_limit"></a>Allow swapchains larger than 4096 px

Allows very large pictures (8K video, theaters) instead of quitting.

- `frame.swapchain_limit` · on by default
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested (on):** Video player (…): creates swapchains larger than 4096 px (8K video, theater textures), which OVRPort's dispatcher aborts on.
- **Suggested (on):** Recommended for every game: OVRPort aborts on swapchains larger than 4096 px; the Frame's runtime handles them.
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `swapchain-size-abort` (fatal): The game crashed creating a very large image (over 4096 px, for example in video players).
- **Source:** [patches/frame/swapchain_limit.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/swapchain_limit.py)

> OVRPort's OpenXR dispatcher aborts the app ('Wrong createInfo size', SIGABRT in libopenxr_loader.so xrCreateSwapchain) when a swapchain is wider or taller than 4096 px, which video players do for 8K video or big theater textures (for example 4XVR). Raises the guard to 16384 px so the Frame's runtime (8192 px max) decides instead.

### <a id="frame-tbxr_vendor"></a>Team Beef ports: treat the Frame as a Meta headset

Lets Team Beef ports (for example Lambda1VR) start on the Frame.

- `frame.tbxr_vendor` · revision 2
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested (on):** Team Beef port: it picks its OpenXR setup by headset maker, which the Frame reports as "valve".
- **Catalog games (1):** Lambda1VR.
- **Source:** [patches/frame/tbxr_vendor.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/tbxr_vendor.py)

> Team Beef's ports (for example Lambda1VR, RTCWQuest) load an OpenXR library named after the headset maker and pick their VR setup by maker; for "valve" they stop at start (libopenxr_loader_valve.so not found) or take the Pico path. Adds that library and lets them take the Meta path. Keeps GL4ES in charge of its desktop OpenGL draw calls so animated models don't turn into stretched triangles.

### <a id="frame-unity_gl_shim"></a>GL shim for Unity (no multisampled render-to-texture)

Stops a gray or frozen screen in Unity games that turn on anti-aliasing while running (for example The Room VR).

- `frame.unity_gl_shim`
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested (on):** Unity GLES game that may switch to MSAA at runtime: hide multisampled render-to-texture, which crashes the Frame's GL driver (for example The Room VR).
- **Catalog games (23):** Audica, BattleSisters, Beat Saber, COMPOUND, Cosmodread, Down the Rabbit Hole, Drunkn Bar Fight, End Space and 15 more.
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `unreal-msrtt-crash` (fatal): The game's graphics crashed a few seconds after start.
- **Source:** [patches/frame/vrapi_bridge.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/vrapi_bridge.py)

> Loads the GL shim into a Unity GLES game and hides GL_EXT_multisampled_render_to_texture (and the multiview variant). Some Unity games switch their eye buffer to 4x MSAA at runtime; the Frame only gives single-sampled swapchains, Unity then renders through multisampled render-to-texture and Mesa/Zink crashes (SIGSEGV in libgallium_dri.so on the render thread: gray or frozen screen, for example The Room VR). Hidden, Unity uses an ordinary MSAA buffer and resolves it. Unity's multiview stays on (gl_hide_multiview defaults to 0 here).

### <a id="frame-unity_multipass"></a>Unity: render each eye separately (no multiview)

Draws each eye separately. Try it when one eye shows a gray or broken picture.

- `frame.unity_multipass` · revision 2
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Catalog games (1):** I Am Cat.
- **Source:** [patches/frame/unity_runtime.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/unity_runtime.py)

> Oculus XR Plugin games render both eyes in one pass (multiview) on Android. If one eye shows only effects or gray (for example I Am Cat), rendering each eye in its own pass can fix it, at some GPU cost. Rewrites OculusSettings.GetStereoRenderingMode and its inlined read in OculusLoader.Initialize -&gt; MultiPass in libil2cpp.so (found with Cpp2IL). Try it when one eye is wrong.

### <a id="frame-unity_no_msaa"></a>Unity: disable MSAA

Turns off a smoothing setting that crashes some older Unity games on the Frame.

- `frame.unity_no_msaa`
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested (on):** Legacy VrApi Unity game on GLES with MSAA (… quality levels): multisampled render-to-texture hangs the Frame's GL driver (for example Sniper Elite VR).
- **Offered (off):** GLES Unity game with MSAA on (… quality levels); enable if it hangs the GPU ('zink: DEVICE LOST').
- **Catalog games (9):** Audica, BattleSisters, Eye of the Temple, IEYTD3, Jurassic World Aftermath Collection, Mini Motor Racing X, Sniper Elite VR, SUPERHOT VR and 1 more.
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `zink-device-lost` (fatal): The GPU hung, so the game froze or closed.
- **Source:** [patches/frame/unity_no_msaa.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/unity_no_msaa.py)

> Sets Unity QualitySettings antiAliasing to 0. Unity's multisampled render-to-texture path can hang the Frame's GL driver ('zink: DEVICE LOST', for example Sniper Elite VR). Try it for GLES Unity games that freeze or crash the GPU.

### <a id="frame-unity_no_overlay_copy"></a>Unity: skip OVROverlay layers (fades, splash screens)

Stops a gray screen crash in some Unity games by skipping their overlay layers (for example The Room VR).

- `frame.unity_no_overlay_copy`
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Catalog games (2):** The Room VR, The Thrill Of The Fight.
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `unity-render-crash` (fatal): The game's graphics crashed, so the picture freezes or stays gray.
- **Source:** [patches/frame/unity_runtime.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/unity_runtime.py)

> Meta's OVROverlay copies a texture into its own compositor layer every frame. For some games (for example The Room VR's screen fade, a 4x4 overlay) that copy crashes the Frame's GL driver: SIGSEGV in libgallium_dri.so on Unity's render thread right after a tiny xrCreateSwapchain, gray or frozen screen. Rewrites OVROverlay.PopulateLayer -&gt; false in libil2cpp.so (found with Cpp2IL): overlays are skipped (fades become instant cuts, overlay splash screens don't show). Only for games with this crash: menus drawn as overlays would disappear too.

### <a id="frame-unity_oculus_check"></a>Unity: start VR without Meta's system apps

Lets older Unity games start VR without Meta's system apps (they'd stay on a 2D screen).

- `frame.unity_oculus_check` · revision 5
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested (on):** Unity with built-in Oculus support: it checks for Meta's system apps before starting VR, else it runs as a 2D app (for example Accounting+, BattleSisters).
- **Catalog games (12):** Accounting+, Audica, BattleSisters, Cosmodread, End Space, Eye of the Temple, Jurassic World Aftermath Collection, Mini Motor Racing X and 4 more.
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `unity-vr-device-none` (fatal): Unity didn't start VR, so the game runs as a hidden 2D app.
- **Source:** [patches/frame/unity_oculus_check.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/unity_oculus_check.py)

> Unity's built-in Oculus support (Unity 2017–2019) only starts VR when Android has Meta's com.oculus.systemactivities package; without it the game runs as a 2D app (the Android home screen or a black window, for example Accounting+, BattleSisters). Points that package name in libunity.so at "android", which always exists. Games on Unity's built-in VR (2017–2018, and 2019 without the Oculus XR Plugin) also get the frame wait their legacy frame loop never makes (libfp_ovrp.so calls ovrp_WaitToBeginFrame before ovrp_Update2; without it no frame starts, the dashboard freezes or the GPU hangs). Per game, the settings ovrp_begin_gate (a freeze at the first scene switch) and ovrp_hold_physics (hands trailing the controllers) switch on two more frame-loop fixes (for example Sniper Elite VR). The shim also counts a newly pressed trigger or A/B/X/Y as a mouse click (Input.GetMouseButtonDown), which Go-era screens wait for (for example Accounting+'s motion warning) and which Lepton never delivers.

### <a id="frame-unity_runtime_msaa_off"></a>Unity: keep MSAA off at runtime (OVRManager)

Keeps a smoothing setting off that the game turns on itself and that can freeze the Frame.

- `frame.unity_runtime_msaa_off` · revision 2
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested (on):** GLES Unity game whose OVRManager turns 4x MSAA on at runtime: multisampled render-to-texture can hang the Frame's GPU.
- **Catalog games (28):** Audica, BattleSisters, Beat Saber, COMPOUND, Cosmodread, Down the Rabbit Hole, Drunkn Bar Fight, End Space and 20 more.
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `unity-render-crash` (fatal): The game's graphics crashed, so the picture freezes or stays gray.
  - `unity-runtime-msaa` (info): The game turns MSAA on at runtime, which can hang the Frame's GPU.
  - `zink-device-lost` (fatal): The GPU hung, so the game froze or closed.
- **Source:** [patches/frame/unity_runtime.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/unity_runtime.py)

> Meta's OVRManager switches Unity to the headset's recommended MSAA level (4x) while the game runs, whatever its quality settings say (log: "Switching to the recommended level"). Multisampled render-to-texture on GLES can hang the Frame's GPU, up to a restart of the whole headset (for example Lucky's Tale in a menu) or a crash of its GL driver (for example The Room VR, whose own code sets 4x). Rewrites OVRDisplay.recommendedMSAALevel -&gt; 0 and makes QualitySettings.antiAliasing's setter do nothing in libil2cpp.so (found with Cpp2IL), so MSAA stays off.

### <a id="frame-unity_text_input"></a>Make Unity text fields work

Lets you type into this app's text fields on the Frame (they'd close at once).

- `frame.unity_text_input` · also for 2D apps
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested (on):** Unity app with text fields (…): they close at once on the Frame because it has no system keyboard.
- **Catalog games (107):** AgeOfJoy, AllInOneSports, Ancient_Dungeon, Arcsmith, Arkio, Assassin's Creed Nexus, Attack on Titan VR: Unbreakable, Audica and 99 more.
- **Source:** [patches/frame/unity_text_input.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/unity_text_input.py)

> Unity's TMP_InputField / InputField wait for Android's on-screen keyboard and close themselves a frame later when there is none (Lepton has no on-screen keyboard; Meta's system keyboard does this on a Quest), so a selected text field only flashes a caret. Rewrites TouchScreenKeyboardShouldBeUsed -&gt; false and isKeyboardUsingEvents (TMP) / InPlaceEditing (uGUI) -&gt; true in libil2cpp.so, found per game with Cpp2IL (downloaded on first use), so fields stay selected and take key presses: Steam's keyboard (with "Show the app window") or Type on Frame from the PC.

### <a id="frame-unity_tls_key_pool"></a>Unity: share thread keys (games that run out of them)

Lets Unity 6 games with many native libraries start when they run out of thread keys (they'd abort with "cannot create thread specific key"), for example Wander.

- `frame.unity_tls_key_pool` · also for 2D apps
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested (on):** Unity 6 with Firebase Firestore and Gecko: these native runtimes can exhaust Android's 128 thread keys alongside the Frame's graphics and XR libraries. Pool Unity's keys to leave room for them.
- **Offered (off):** Unity 6 with …: turn on if the game aborts at start with "cannot create thread specific key" (for example Wander).
- **Catalog games (1):** Wander.
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `pthread-keys-exhausted` (fatal): The game ran out of thread keys (Android allows 128 per process; Unity 6 plus large native libraries such as Firebase or Gecko, and the Frame's own graphics/OpenXR libraries, use them up), so a library aborted at start (for example Wander in Firebase's Firestore).
- **Source:** [patches/frame/unity_tls_key_pool.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/unity_tls_key_pool.py)

> Android gives a process 128 thread keys (pthread keys, per-thread storage slots). Unity 6 takes about 40, and on the Frame the graphics and OpenXR libraries take more than on a Quest, so games with many other native libraries run out: Wander aborted at start ("cannot create thread specific key" in Firebase). Unity's keys without a clean-up function become slots behind one real key (libfp_tkeys.so); every other key and every other library keep real ones. Approach by Klownicle (GitHub #198).

### <a id="frame-unity_user_presence"></a>Unity: headset always counts as worn

Counts the headset as worn, so games that only move the player while it's worn get head tracking and controls (for example BONELAB).

- `frame.unity_user_presence`
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Catalog games (1):** BONELAB.
- **Source:** [patches/frame/unity_user_presence.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/unity_user_presence.py)

> Unity's Oculus XR Plugin asks OVRPlugin whether the headset is worn; on the Frame the answer turns to "not worn" a few seconds after start. Games that only move the player while the headset is worn then show a frozen body with no head tracking and no controls (for example BONELAB). Reports the headset as worn; taking it off still pauses the game through the session's focus.

### <a id="frame-unreal_gl_shim"></a>GL shim for Unreal (no multisampled render-to-texture)

Stops a crash a few seconds after start in some Unreal games with anti-aliasing (for example Star Wars Pinball VR).

- `frame.unreal_gl_shim`
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Catalog games (1):** Star Wars Pinball VR.
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `unreal-msrtt-crash` (fatal): The game's graphics crashed a few seconds after start.
- **Source:** [patches/frame/vrapi_bridge.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/vrapi_bridge.py)

> Loads the GL shim into an Unreal GLES game and hides GL_EXT_multisampled_render_to_texture. Unreal's mobile MSAA renders through multisampled render-to-texture, and the Frame's GL driver (Mesa/Zink) can crash on it: SIGSEGV with fault address 0x10000 in libgallium_dri.so on the RHIThread a few seconds after start (Zink looks up a render-pass cache slot past its end, for example Star Wars Pinball VR). Hidden, Unreal renders without that path. Unreal's multiview stays on: Unreal only uses it when GL_OVR_multiview_multisampled_render_to_texture is listed too, so for Unreal the shim keeps that one visible and draws its multiview MSAA attachments single-sampled (glFramebufferTextureMultiviewOVR).

### <a id="frame-unreal_multiview_depth"></a>Unreal: match multiview depth to the eye size

Shows the full environment when its upper part is clipped but menu panels look correct.

- `frame.unreal_multiview_depth`
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Catalog games (1):** Star Wars: Tales from the Galaxy's Edge.
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `unreal-multiview-depth-size` (warning): The measured multiview depth attachment keeps the initial Android window dimensions and clips the taller eye color target (Tales from the Galaxy's Edge, issue 61).
- **Source:** [patches/frame/unreal_multiview_depth.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/unreal_multiview_depth.py)

> Some UE4 games keep the initial Android window size for their stereo depth buffer, clipping the upper part of the environment while menu panels look correct. Refreshes the cached depth dimensions from the current eye render target before allocation. Preserves multiview and multisampling. Verified in Tales from the Galaxy's Edge 1.1.9; changes one branch only when the function size and surrounding code match.

### <a id="frame-unreal_ovrp_entrypoints"></a>Unreal: stand-ins for OVRPlugin functions OVRPort lacks

Lets older Unreal games start VR on the Frame (for example Star Wars Pinball VR).

- `frame.unreal_ovrp_entrypoints`
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested (on):** Unreal looks up OVRPlugin function(s) OVRPort's OVRPlugin lacks: ……. Without them Unreal starts no VR.
- **Catalog games (2):** Ghostbusters: Rise of the Ghost Lord, Star Wars Pinball VR.
- **Source:** [patches/frame/unreal_ovrp.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/unreal_ovrp.py)

> Unreal's Oculus module looks up every OVRPlugin function it was built against and starts no VR when one is missing; OVRPort's OpenXR OVRPlugin lacks some old ones (for example ovrp_GetPTWNear, which Unreal 4.25 builds like Star Wars Pinball VR look up). The game then never starts an OpenXR session and crashes a few seconds in. Adds a generated library to libOVRPlugin.so with a stand-in for each missing function that reports failure (ovrpFailure), so Unreal's Oculus support starts. The functions OVRPort has are untouched.

### <a id="frame-unreal_quest_keymap"></a>Unreal: Quest controller bindings (RPOC key map)

Makes grip, trigger and touch controls reach the game's hands (it picked the empty Gear VR controls on the Frame, for example Vader Immortal).

- `frame.unreal_quest_keymap`
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Catalog games (3):** Vader Immortal: Episode I, Vader Immortal: Episode II, Vader Immortal: Episode III.
- **Source:** [patches/frame/unreal_santacruz.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/unreal_santacruz.py)

> ILMxLAB's Unreal games (for example Vader Immortal) bind their controls through URPOCKeyMapManagerComponent, which for an Oculus headset picks the Quest ("SantaCruz") or the Gear VR key set by IsRunningOnSantaCruz. On the Frame it picks Gear VR, which is empty in a Quest build: grip, trigger and touch reach Unreal but never the game's hands (grabbing does nothing). Removes the branch to the Gear VR set in the Oculus case of the key selector both action and axis mappings use. Found by Klownicle (GitHub #49).

### <a id="frame-unreal_quest_precompile"></a>Unreal: don't wait for the Quest shader precompile

Lets the game leave its loading screen: it waited for a Quest-only step that never starts on the Frame (for example Vader Immortal).

- `frame.unreal_quest_precompile`
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Catalog games (3):** Vader Immortal: Episode I, Vader Immortal: Episode II, Vader Immortal: Episode III.
- **Source:** [patches/frame/unreal_santacruz.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/unreal_santacruz.py)

> ILMxLAB's Unreal games (for example Vader Immortal) wait on their loading card until UVRUtils::GetQuestShaderPrecompilePercent reaches 100 %. The precompile only starts on a Quest (IsRunningOnSantaCruz); on any other device the function returns 0.0, so the loading card (a portrait with a progress bar) never ends. Makes that non-Quest branch return 1.0. The Quest branch and the game's normal shader compiling stay as they are. Found by Klownicle (GitHub #49).

### <a id="frame-unreal_skip_obb_check"></a>Unreal: start without the OBB check

Starts Unreal games without re-checking their data file (they'd seem to hang on an invisible check screen).

- `frame.unreal_skip_obb_check` · also for 2D apps
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested (on):** Unreal checks the OBB's contents before starting (bVerifyOBBOnStartUp); on the Frame a failed or slow check can't be seen and the game seems to hang.
- **Catalog games (6):** Dance Central, Kill It With Fire VR, Lost Recipes, MacacoVR, Maestro, Ragnarock.
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `unreal-obb-check-stuck` (fatal): The game stays on Unreal's OBB check screen (DownloaderActivity), which the Frame doesn't show, and never starts VR (for example Contractors, GitHub #159).
- **Source:** [patches/frame/unreal_obb_check.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/unreal_obb_check.py)

> Unreal games can check their whole data file (.obb) before starting (bVerifyOBBOnStartUp). On the Frame that check's progress and error screens are invisible (Lepton runs VR games without an Android window), so the game seems to hang on its DownloaderActivity, for example Contractors. This turns the check off in the manifest; Unreal still checks that the OBB is there with the right size, so a missing or wrong-version OBB still stops the game.

### <a id="frame-unreal_skip_obb_delivery"></a>Unreal: skip the OBB delivery check

Skips a separate data-file check when an Unreal game still hangs at startup with the content check off. Experimental; the game still needs its data.

- `frame.unreal_skip_obb_delivery` · experimental · also for 2D apps
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Catalog games (1):** Medal of Honor: Above and Beyond.
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `unreal-obb-check-stuck` (fatal): The game stays on Unreal's OBB check screen (DownloaderActivity), which the Frame doesn't show, and never starts VR (for example Contractors, GitHub #159).
- **Source:** [patches/frame/unreal_obb_check.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/unreal_obb_check.py)

> Unreal's Java OBB delivery check can leave a game on an invisible DownloaderActivity screen even with the manifest CRC check off (e.g. Into The Radius). Makes known Unreal delivery predicates return true, including recognized obfuscated versions, bypassing the Java name and size gate. Experimental: the native engine still needs complete, matching, readable OBB data.

### <a id="frame-unreal_splash_bypass"></a>Unreal: bypass the stalled loading splash

Lets the game finish loading when its separate loading splash stalls the render thread.

- `frame.unreal_splash_bypass`
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Catalog games (1):** Star Wars: Tales from the Galaxy's Edge.
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `unreal-splash-frame-stall` (error): Unreal's map loading waits for rendering while its separate Oculus splash waits for an unbegun VR frame (Tales from the Galaxy's Edge, issue 61).
- **Source:** [patches/frame/unreal_splash.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/unreal_splash.py)

> Some UE4 Oculus games stall during map loading: the game waits for the render thread, and the separate loading splash waits for an unbegun VR frame. Bypasses the splash renderer so loading finishes; the last image stays visible during loading. The normal environment and menu rendering continue. Verified in Tales from the Galaxy's Edge 1.1.9; changes one instruction only when the function size and prologue match.

### <a id="frame-unreal_thumb_touch"></a>Unreal: thumb follows the capacitive touches

Makes the hands' thumbs follow what your thumb touches (they always pointed up: the Frame doesn't sense a thumb hovering, for example Vader Immortal).

- `frame.unreal_thumb_touch`
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Catalog games (7):** Phantom: Covert Ops, Robo Recall, Star Wars: Tales from the Galaxy's Edge, Time Stall, Vader Immortal: Episode I, Vader Immortal: Episode II, Vader Immortal: Episode III.
- **Source:** [patches/frame/unreal_thumb_touch.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/unreal_thumb_touch.py)

> Unreal 4's Oculus input sets the ThumbUp axis (games animate the hand's thumb with it) from Meta's near-touch sensing, which the Frame never reports: the thumb always points up. Uses the touches instead (left X/Y/stick/thumb rest, right A/B/stick/thumb rest). Changes three instructions in OculusInput::SendControllerEvents, only where the code matches exactly (UE4 Oculus games of one engine generation, for example Vader Immortal, Robo Recall). Found by Klownicle (GitHub #49).

### <a id="frame-vermillion_scene_canvas"></a>Vermillion: paint canvases in the scene

Keeps the hand and brush visible over Vermillion's painting canvas (the canvas is drawn in the scene instead of as a layer in front).

- `frame.vermillion_scene_canvas`
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Catalog games (1):** Vermillion.
- **Source:** [patches/frame/vermillion_canvas.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/vermillion_canvas.py)

> Vermillion shows a canvas being painted as a separate compositor layer, which the Frame draws in front of everything: the hand and brush disappear over the canvas while they still paint. Rewrites PaintableMesh.HasCompositorLayerAvailable and ShouldUseCompositorOverlay -&gt; false in libil2cpp.so (found with Cpp2IL), so the game uses its own fallback and draws the canvas in the scene. The canvas may look a little less sharp.

### <a id="frame-vivox_audio_route"></a>Vivox voice chat: skip Android 12 audio routing

Lets games with Vivox voice chat start on the Frame (they'd crash on an Android 12 audio call).

- `frame.vivox_audio_route` · also for 2D apps
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested (on):** Vivox voice chat: it calls Android 12 audio methods, which Lepton (Android 11) lacks, and crashes.
- **Catalog games (2):** Dungeons of Eternity, Real VR Fishing.
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `vivox-api31` (fatal): The game's Vivox voice-chat SDK calls Android 12 audio-routing methods (AudioManager communication devices) without checking the Android version; Lepton runs Android 11, so the app crashes (for example Green Hell VR).
- **Source:** [patches/frame/vivox_audio_route.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/vivox_audio_route.py)

> Vivox's voice-chat SDK (for example Green Hell VR) checks the audio route with Android 12 methods (AudioManager communication devices) without checking the Android version; Lepton runs Android 11, so the game crashes at start with a NoSuchMethodError. Those Vivox methods return at once instead (an in-place edit of classes.dex); voice chat keeps the default audio route.

### <a id="frame-vk_sanitize"></a>Vulkan: drop invalid render-pass pointers

Cleans up graphics data that crashes some Unreal games on the Frame.

- `frame.vk_sanitize` · on by default
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested (on):** Own-engine game: applied when one of its libraries loads Vulkan by name (for example Roblox); keeps Lepton's Fossilize layer from crashing on uninitialized pointers.
- **Suggested (on):** Unreal game: applied automatically when the engine loads Vulkan by name; keeps Lepton's Fossilize layer from crashing on uninitialized pointers (for example Deadpool VR).
- **Catalog games (1):** WiiCompiled VR.
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `fossilize-renderpass` (fatal): A Vulkan layer in Lepton (Fossilize) crashed while the game set up its graphics.
  - `unreal-vulkan-driver-crash` (fatal): The Frame's Vulkan driver crashed on a call from Unreal.
- **Source:** [patches/frame/vk_sanitize.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/vk_sanitize.py)

> Some engines leave the pNext of unused Vulkan attachment references uninitialized. The Frame's driver never reads it, but Lepton always loads Steam's Fossilize shader-cache layer, which follows it and crashes on the first frame (SIGSEGV in libVkLayer_fossilize.so from FVulkanRenderPass, for example Deadpool VR). Loads Vulkan through a small shim that keeps valid pointers and drops only unreadable ones or ones pointing at the wrong structure type. It also drops a depth resolve named in a subpass without a depth attachment, which crashes the Frame's driver at the first render pass (for example Metro Awakening).

### <a id="frame-vrapi_bridge"></a>VrApi → OpenXR bridge

Lets games built on Meta's oldest VR interface run on the Frame.

- `frame.vrapi_bridge` · experimental
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested (on):** The engine calls libvrapi.so directly; OVRPort can't translate it.
- **Conflicts with:** [`frame.vrapi_stub`](#frame-vrapi_stub)
- **Catalog games (4):** BlazeRush, Path of the Warrior, The Climb, The Climb 2.
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `direct-vrapi` (warning): The game uses Meta's VrApi directly and needs the VrApi bridge.
  - `vrapi-frame-rejected` (fatal): The VrApi bridge rejected the game's frame options, so no picture reaches the headset even though frame pacing can appear in the log.
- **Source:** [patches/frame/vrapi_bridge.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/vrapi_bridge.py)

> Replaces libvrapi.so with a VrApi→OpenXR bridge (Android-XR-Bridge/OVRPort fork, GPL-3.0, patched for the Frame: GLES sessions, cylinder→quad layers, sRGB format fallback, 30 s VR-mode deadline, emulated time conversion). Needed when the engine calls VrApi itself instead of through OVRPlugin (for example The Climb 2, Path of the Warrior); OVRPort cannot translate those.

### <a id="frame-vrapi_stub"></a>Quiet Meta's VrApi loader (OpenXR games)

Stops Meta's old VR library from closing the game at start (for example Jurassic World Aftermath).

- `frame.vrapi_stub`
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Conflicts with:** [`frame.vrapi_bridge`](#frame-vrapi_bridge)
- **Catalog games (2):** Jurassic World Aftermath Collection, ZombielandVR.
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `vrapi-before-init` (fatal): Meta's VrApi loader stopped the game.
- **Source:** [patches/frame/vrapi_stub.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/vrapi_stub.py)

> Some OpenXR games still ship Meta's VrApi loader and call it a few times without starting VrApi (for example Jurassic World Aftermath); Meta's loader then stops the game ("vrapi_SetPropertyInt was called before vrapi_Initialize()"). Replaces it with a library that has the same functions, each doing nothing. Only for games whose VR runs through OVRPlugin on OpenXR.

### <a id="frame-zink_shader_fix"></a>OpenGL ES: shader fixes (Vulkan layer under Zink)

Repairs shaders that hang the graphics chip at certain effects, from the game's recipe (for example Vader Immortal's lightspeed jump).

- `frame.zink_shader_fix`
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Catalog games (1):** Vader Immortal: Episode I.
- **Source:** [patches/frame/zink_shader_fix.py](../src/frameport/patches/frame/zink_shader_fix.py)

> Loads FramePort's shader-fix Vulkan layer into an OpenGL ES game. On the Frame, OpenGL ES runs on Zink (Mesa's GL on Vulkan); the layer sits between Zink and the driver and inserts the words of the adapter setting zink_shader_fix into the SPIR-V modules whose size and SHA-256 match (every other module is untouched), for example stores that set loop counters and accumulators a shader reads before writing, which hang the GPU (Vader Immortal's lightspeed jump; found by Klownicle, GitHub #49). Does nothing without zink_shader_fix (or zink_shader_dump) in the recipe. The layer adds itself to Android's Vulkan debug layer list for the game's process only.

## <a id="group-adapter"></a>Game settings

Settings of FrameBridge, FramePort's OpenXR layer inside every converted Quest game. Most can be changed on the Frame later without a rebuild (game page → Game settings).

### <a id="adapter-aim_forward"></a>Pointer start

Moves where the pointer starts, forward or back.

- `adapter.aim_forward`
- **Changes:** Game setting: stored in the build and on the Frame (settings.conf); can be changed without a rebuild.
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Options:**
  - Value: float, default `0.0`.
  - Game settings → Controllers → "Pointer start" (advanced): slider -0.3–0.3 in steps of 0.01.
- **Source:** [patches/settings.py](../src/frameport/patches/settings.py)

> Moves where the pointing ray starts forward (+) or back (−).

### <a id="adapter-aim_pitch"></a>Pointer angle

If the pointer doesn't hit what you aim at, tilt it up or down.

- `adapter.aim_pitch`
- **Changes:** Game setting: stored in the build and on the Frame (settings.conf); can be changed without a rebuild.
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Options:**
  - Value: float, default `0.0`.
  - Game settings → Controllers → "Pointer angle": slider -30–30 in steps of 1.
- **Source:** [patches/settings.py](../src/frameport/patches/settings.py)

> Tilts the controllers' pointing ray up (+) or down (−), for games whose pointer doesn't hit what you aim at.

### <a id="adapter-aim_yaw"></a>Pointer turn

Turns the pointer left or right.

- `adapter.aim_yaw`
- **Changes:** Game setting: stored in the build and on the Frame (settings.conf); can be changed without a rebuild.
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Options:**
  - Value: float, default `0.0`.
  - Game settings → Controllers → "Pointer turn" (advanced): slider -30–30 in steps of 1.
- **Source:** [patches/settings.py](../src/frameport/patches/settings.py)

> Turns the controllers' pointing ray left (+) or right (−).

### <a id="adapter-controller_fix"></a>Use controllers

Turn off only for games you play with your hands instead of controllers.

- `adapter.controller_fix`
- **Changes:** Game setting: stored in the build and on the Frame (settings.conf); can be changed without a rebuild.
- **Suggested (on), value `0`:** Hand tracking is required by the game: pass hands through instead of reporting Touch controllers (for example Silhouette).
- **Options:**
  - Value: int, default `1` (always written).
  - Game settings → Controllers → "Use controllers".
- **Catalog games (1):** Silhouette.
- **Source:** [patches/settings.py](../src/frameport/patches/settings.py)

> Reports Frame controllers as Oculus Touch and hides synthetic hand tracking. Set 0 for games that require hand tracking (for example Silhouette).

### <a id="adapter-controller_models"></a>Show Steam Frame controllers

For games that show the headset's own controllers. Takes effect after a reinstall.

- `adapter.controller_models`
- **Changes:** Game setting, stored in the build: needs a rebuild.
- **Suggested (on), value `1`:** The game asks the headset for its controller models: show Steam Frame controllers instead of Quest Touch controllers.
- **Options:**
  - Value: int, default `0`.
  - Game settings → Controllers → "Show Steam Frame controllers".
- **Catalog games (6):** Neko Atsume Purrfect, Ocean Rift, Real VR Fishing, SynthRiders, VR HOT Quest, Walkabout Mini Golf.
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `render-model-requested` (info): The game shows Quest controllers (or none) because the Frame doesn't provide controller models.
- **Source:** [patches/settings.py](../src/frameport/patches/settings.py)

> Games that ask the headset for its controller models (Meta's runtime controller models, XR_FB_render_model) get the Steam Frame controllers instead of Quest Touch controllers. The models come from the Frame's own SteamVR and are converted on the Frame at install time. Games that ship their own controller meshes aren't affected. Turning it on needs a rebuild (it adds a small library in front of OVRPort's loader).

### <a id="adapter-cube_standin"></a>Stand in for cube layers

Keeps games running that use a 360° cube layer the Frame lacks (for example Budget Cuts Ultimate). Leave it on.

- `adapter.cube_standin`
- **Changes:** Game setting: stored in the build and on the Frame (settings.conf); can be changed without a rebuild.
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Options:**
  - Value: int, default `1`.
  - Game settings → Troubleshooting → "Stand in for cube layers" (advanced).
- **Source:** [patches/settings.py](../src/frameport/patches/settings.py)

> The Frame's runtime has no cube-map layers and refuses their swapchains; OVRPlugin then crashes when it submits the next frame (for example Budget Cuts Ultimate). FrameBridge serves such a swapchain itself (a GL cube map, GLES games) and drops its layers, so the game runs on without that layer.

### <a id="adapter-cylinder_strips"></a>Show curved menus and screens

The Frame can't show curved panels; this shows them as gently bent strips.

- `adapter.cylinder_strips`
- **Changes:** Game setting: stored in the build and on the Frame (settings.conf); can be changed without a rebuild.
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Options:**
  - Value: int, default `1`.
  - Game settings → Menus and screens → "Show curved menus and screens".
- **Source:** [patches/settings.py](../src/frameport/patches/settings.py)

> Cylinder layers (curved menus and movie screens, for example 4XVR), which the Frame's runtime lacks, are shown as a few flat strips along the curve. 0 = drop them. 360° (equirect) layers can't be shown on the Frame.

### <a id="adapter-equirect_emul"></a>Show 360° backgrounds and videos

Video players' virtual theaters and 360° videos would otherwise stay black.

- `adapter.equirect_emul`
- **Changes:** Game setting: stored in the build and on the Frame (settings.conf); can be changed without a rebuild.
- **Suggested (on), value `1`:** The game draws 360° layers (for example a video player's theater or 360° videos), which the Frame's runtime can't show: show them as panels around you.
- **Options:**
  - Value: int, default `0`.
  - Game settings → 360° pictures and video → "Show 360° backgrounds and videos".
- **Catalog games (5):** 4XVR Video Player, Into The Radius 2, Pinball FX VR, Riven, Tea For God.
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `equirect-layers-dropped` (warning): The game's 360° pictures (for example a video player's theater or 360° videos) are missing because the Frame's runtime can't show equirect layers.
- **Source:** [patches/settings.py](../src/frameport/patches/settings.py)

> 360° (equirect) layers, for example a video player's virtual theater or 360° videos (for example 4XVR), which the Frame's runtime lacks, are drawn by a background thread into a layer behind the game's own picture: the 360° image is converted only when it changes (a theater once, a 360° video once per video frame) and the view is drawn for each frame's head pose. GLES games only; without it these layers are missing (black).

### <a id="adapter-equirect_face"></a>360° detail

Higher keeps more detail but uses more memory.

- `adapter.equirect_face`
- **Changes:** Game setting: stored in the build and on the Frame (settings.conf); can be changed without a rebuild.
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Options:**
  - Value: int, default `1536`.
  - Game settings → 360° pictures and video → "360° detail" (advanced): Low (`1024`), Normal (`1536`), High (`2048`), Maximum (`2730`); shown while `adapter.equirect_emul` is on.
- **Source:** [patches/settings.py](../src/frameport/patches/settings.py)

> Maximum size in pixels of each face of the cube the 360° image is converted to (256–2730). Higher is sharper but uses more GPU memory.

### <a id="adapter-equirect_flip"></a>360° picture orientation

Only if 360° pictures show wrongly.

- `adapter.equirect_flip`
- **Changes:** Game setting: stored in the build and on the Frame (settings.conf); can be changed without a rebuild.
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Options:**
  - Value: int, default `0`.
  - Game settings → 360° pictures and video → "360° picture orientation" (advanced): Normal (`0`), Upside down (`1`), Mirrored (`2`), Upside down and mirrored (`3`), Turned around (`4`); shown while `adapter.equirect_emul` is on.
- **Source:** [patches/settings.py](../src/frameport/patches/settings.py)

> Only if 360° pictures show wrongly: 1 = upside down, 2 = mirrored, 4 = turned around (add values to combine).

### <a id="adapter-equirect_fps"></a>360° video frame rate limit

Must be at least the video's own frame rate.

- `adapter.equirect_fps`
- **Changes:** Game setting: stored in the build and on the Frame (settings.conf); can be changed without a rebuild.
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Options:**
  - Value: float, default `60.0`.
  - Game settings → 360° pictures and video → "360° video frame rate limit" (advanced): No limit (`0`), 24 (`24`), 30 (`30`), 60 (`60`), 90 (`90`); shown while `adapter.equirect_emul` is on.
- **Source:** [patches/settings.py](../src/frameport/patches/settings.py)

> At most this many redraws per second of a 360° layer (0 = no limit). Video players need at least the video's frame rate.

### <a id="adapter-equirect_res"></a>360° sharpness

Higher is sharper but needs more power.

- `adapter.equirect_res`

- **Source:** [patches/settings.py](../src/frameport/patches/settings.py)

> Size in pixels per eye of the 360° background, redrawn every frame on a background thread (512–4096). Higher is sharper but costs more GPU time per frame.

### <a id="adapter-gl_highp_markers"></a>GL shim: high-precision vertex shaders

Computes some of the game's effects more precisely, so they don't draw streaks or flashes (for example BlazeRush's particles). Comes from a game's recipe.

- `adapter.gl_highp_markers` · revision 2
- **Changes:** Game setting: stored in the build and on the Frame (settings.conf); can be changed without a rebuild.
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Options:**
  - Value: str, default empty.
  - Not in the Game settings dialog (set by a recipe or the CLI).
- **Catalog games (1):** BlazeRush.
- **Source:** [patches/settings.py](../src/frameport/patches/settings.py)

> GL shim (frame.gl_shim): vertex shaders whose source contains every '\|'-separated text compute in highp: whole-word mediump becomes highp on every line without the words in, out or uniform (the shader's interface keeps its precision). For effects that draw streaks or flashes from mediump rounding on the Frame (for example BlazeRush's particles: in uvec2 inBoneIndices;\|uniform InstanceData\|void main()). Pair it with a new shader cache name if the game caches compiled programs. Comes from a game's recipe.

### <a id="adapter-gl_int_attribs"></a>GL shim: integer vertex inputs

Shows models whose shapes come from bone data the Frame's graphics driver misreads (for example BlazeRush's cars). Comes from a game's recipe.

- `adapter.gl_int_attribs` · revision 2
- **Changes:** Game setting: stored in the build and on the Frame (settings.conf); can be changed without a rebuild.
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Options:**
  - Value: int, default `0`.
  - Not in the Game settings dialog (set by a recipe or the CLI).
- **Catalog games (1):** BlazeRush.
- **Source:** [patches/settings.py](../src/frameport/patches/settings.py)

> GL shim (frame.gl_shim): shader inputs declared as integers (int/uint, ivecN/uvecN) whose vertex data the game set up with glVertexAttribPointer (as floats) are set up again with glVertexAttribIPointer before each draw. Qualcomm's Quest driver read the raw integers anyway; the Frame's GL driver converts them to floats, so skinned models using bone indices vanish (for example BlazeRush's car bodies and controllers; Klownicle's guide, GitHub #57). Comes from a game's recipe.
