### <a id="adapter-haptic_fix"></a>Fix freezes when controllers vibrate

For games that freeze the Frame when a controller vibrates (for example Lucky's Tale). Needs a rebuild.

- `adapter.haptic_fix` · revision 2
- **Changes:** Game setting, stored in the build: needs a rebuild.
- **Suggested (on), value `1`:** Meta's OVRPlugin vibrates controllers through OVRPort's loader, which turns some vibrations into gigabyte allocations that freeze the Frame (for example Lucky's Tale, BattleSisters): vibrations are converted before they reach it.
- **Options:**
  - Value: int, default `0`.
  - Game settings → Controllers → "Fix freezes when controllers vibrate" (advanced).
- **Catalog games (88):** AgeOfJoy, Ancient_Dungeon, Attack on Titan VR: Unbreakable, Audica, AugmentedEmpire, Battlemarked, BattleSisters, Beat Saber and 80 more.
- **Source:** [patches/settings.py](../src/frameport/patches/settings.py)

> Routes OVRPlugin through FramePort's extension shim, which turns Meta's amplitude-envelope vibrations into plain ones: OVRPort's loader reads their nanosecond duration as seconds and allocates gigabytes, freezing the Frame when the game vibrates a controller (for example Lucky's Tale's save slots, GitHub #9). Needs a rebuild.

### <a id="adapter-pose_time_fix"></a>Fix hands lagging behind controllers

For games whose hands trail the controllers when you move them (for example BattleSisters).

- `adapter.pose_time_fix`
- **Changes:** Game setting: stored in the build and on the Frame (settings.conf); can be changed without a rebuild.
- **Suggested (on), value `1`:** Unity's built-in Oculus support reads controller poses through OVRPlugin at its monotonic "now", seconds in the past on the Frame: they are located at the right time (for example BattleSisters, Sniper Elite VR).
- **Suggested (on), value `1`:** Unreal 4's Oculus input of this OVRPlugin generation asks for controller poses at OVRPlugin's own clock, which is behind the Frame's: they are located at the right time (for example Vader Immortal).
- **Options:**
  - Value: int, default `0`.
  - Game settings → Controllers → "Fix hands lagging behind controllers" (advanced).
- **Catalog games (14):** Battlemarked, BattleSisters, Beat Saber, Dance Central, Dungeons of Eternity, Mini Motor Racing X, Phantom: Covert Ops, Quantum Void and 6 more.
- **Source:** [patches/settings.py](../src/frameport/patches/settings.py)

> Poses a game asks for at a CLOCK_MONOTONIC time, or more than 0.5 s before the frame's display time, are located at the same moment in the runtime's time (or now). Meta's OVRPlugin passes the monotonic clock on as the OpenXR time, which on the Frame runs seconds behind the runtime's clock, so its "now" poses (Unity's physics step, controller poses) came from the past: hands trailing the controllers (for example BattleSisters, Sniper Elite VR).

Without it such apps get no controller input.

- **Options:**
  - Value: int, default `0`.
  - Game settings → Controllers → "Animate fingers from touch" (advanced): Off (`0`), Thumbs (`1`), Thumbs and index fingers (`2`).
- **Source:** [patches/settings.py](../src/frameport/patches/settings.py)

> Meta's OVRPlugin reports a thumb (or index finger) resting near the controller through XR_FB_touch_controller_proximity, which the Frame's runtime lacks: "near" stays false and games that animate the hands from it show a thumb that never moves (for example Vader Immortal; found by Klownicle, GitHub #49). Binds the game's proximity actions to the capacitive touch inputs instead: 1 = thumb (thumbstick, face buttons or thumb rest touched), 2 = also the index finger (trigger touched). Only when the runtime lacks the extension.

### <a id="adapter-rect_clamp"></a>Keep pictures in bounds

Stops games from hanging when their eye picture is a little too big (for example PowerWash Simulator). Leave it on.

- `adapter.rect_clamp`
- **Changes:** Game setting: stored in the build and on the Frame (settings.conf); can be changed without a rebuild.
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Options:**
  - Value: int, default `1`.
  - Game settings → Troubleshooting → "Keep pictures in bounds" (advanced).
- **Source:** [patches/settings.py](../src/frameport/patches/settings.py)

> Keeps every submitted image rect inside its swapchain. Unity can size the eye area a few pixels past the image on some Frames; SteamVR then rejects every frame (xrEndFrame -25, XR_ERROR_SWAPCHAIN_RECT_INVALID) and the game stops drawing (for example PowerWash Simulator stuck at "Waiting").

### <a id="adapter-refresh_rate"></a>Refresh rate

How often the picture updates. Higher is smoother if the game can keep up.

- `adapter.refresh_rate`
- **Changes:** Game setting: stored in the build and on the Frame (settings.conf); can be changed without a rebuild.
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Options:**
  - Value: float, default `0.0`.
  - Game settings → Picture → "Refresh rate": Game's choice (`0`), 72 Hz (`72`), 80 Hz (`80`), 90 Hz (`90`), 96 Hz (`96`), 108 Hz (`108`), 120 Hz (`120`), 144 Hz (`144`).
- **Catalog games (3):** Does it Stack?, Majora's Mask VR, Vacation Simulator.
- **Source:** [patches/settings.py](../src/frameport/patches/settings.py)

> Display refresh rate for this game (72, 80, 90, 96, 108, 120 or 144; 0 = the game's choice). A video's frame rate that divides the refresh rate plays smoothest (for example 30 fps at 90 Hz, 24 fps at 72 Hz).

### <a id="adapter-release_wait"></a>Wait for the game's GPU

For games where one eye flickers or jitters. Costs some speed.

- `adapter.release_wait`
- **Changes:** Game setting: stored in the build and on the Frame (settings.conf); can be changed without a rebuild.
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Options:**
  - Value: int, default `0`.
  - Game settings → Troubleshooting → "Wait for the game's GPU" (advanced).
- **Source:** [patches/settings.py](../src/frameport/patches/settings.py)

> Before a swapchain image is handed to the Frame, wait until the game's GPU work on it has finished, for games that hand over images early (an eye flickers or jitters). Costs some frame time. 2 = only after the first 60 s (compare both in one session).

Without it these panels are missing and a game waiting for its video stays black. 0 = leave them to the runtime.

### <a id="adapter-sync_guard"></a>Steady controller input after focus

For games that crash right after you return to them (for example after the Steam menu).

- `adapter.sync_guard`
- **Changes:** Game setting: stored in the build and on the Frame (settings.conf); can be changed without a rebuild.
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Options:**
  - Value: int, default `0`.
  - Game settings → Troubleshooting → "Steady controller input after focus" (advanced).
- **Catalog games (3):** Batman: Arkham Shadow, Myst, Robo Recall.
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `runtime-input-crash` (fatal): The Frame's runtime crashed in its controller code, usually right after the game got focus. sync_guard runs input syncs (xrSyncActions) one at a time and pauses them briefly after focus returns.
- **Source:** [patches/settings.py](../src/frameport/patches/settings.py)

> Runs xrSyncActions one at a time with xrPollEvent and skips it for 250 ms after focus returns. For games that crash in the runtime's input code right after focus comes back (SIGSEGV in vrclient.so UpdateActionStateInternal / xrSyncActions, for example Myst).

### <a id="adapter-vk_hide_fdm"></a>Hide Vulkan foveation

For Unreal Engine 5 games that crash on the Frame (for example Metro Awakening).

- `adapter.vk_hide_fdm`
- **Changes:** Game setting: stored in the build and on the Frame (settings.conf); can be changed without a rebuild.
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Options:**
  - Value: int, default `0`.
  - Game settings → Troubleshooting → "Hide Vulkan foveation" (advanced).
- **Catalog games (1):** Metro Awakening.
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `unreal-fdm-missing` (warning): The game will likely crash a few seconds in: Unreal expects foveation data the Frame doesn't provide.
  - `unreal-vulkan-driver-crash` (fatal): The Frame's Vulkan driver crashed on a call from Unreal.
- **Source:** [patches/settings.py](../src/frameport/patches/settings.py)

> Vulkan shim (frame.vk_sanitize): the game doesn't see VK_EXT_fragment_density_map(2). Unreal Engine 5 turns on fragment-density-map foveation when the driver offers it and expects the density map from the headset, which the Frame doesn't provide: image views and barriers for a missing image, then a crash in the Frame's Vulkan driver (for example Metro Awakening). Valve's own foveation layer isn't affected.

### <a id="adapter-vk_query_slots"></a>Stop objects popping in and out

For Vulkan games whose models flicker or vanish while you look at them (for example Into The Radius 2). Needs a rebuild.

- `adapter.vk_query_slots` · revision 3
- **Changes:** Game setting, stored in the build: needs a rebuild.
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Options:**
  - Value: int, default `0`.
  - Game settings → Troubleshooting → "Stop objects popping in and out" (advanced).
- **Source:** [patches/settings.py](../src/frameport/patches/settings.py)

> Vulkan shim (frame.vk_sanitize): on gives every occlusion query room for both eyes. In multiview passes the Frame's driver writes a zero result for the second eye into the next query, so engines that count on one slot cull visible objects (models popping in and out, for example Into The Radius 2). 0 = off, 1 = on (2 slots).

### <a id="adapter-vk_shader_dump"></a>Vulkan shader dump (diagnostics)

Saves the game's shaders to find one that hangs the GPU. No effect on the game.

- `adapter.vk_shader_dump`
- **Changes:** Game setting: stored in the build and on the Frame (settings.conf); can be changed without a rebuild.
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Options:**
  - Value: int, default `0`.
  - Game settings → Troubleshooting → "Vulkan shader dump (diagnostics)" (advanced).
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `gpu-hang` (fatal): The Frame's GPU hung while the game ran (the kernel reset it; the game froze or closed).
- **Source:** [patches/settings.py](../src/frameport/patches/settings.py)

> Vulkan shim (frame.vk_sanitize): writes every distinct SPIR-V module the game creates to Android/data/&lt;package&gt;/files/fp_vk_shaders/&lt;size&gt;_&lt;sha256&gt;.spv, with index.txt listing every creation in order with its time, to find the shader behind a GPU hang and capture it for a new vk_shader_fix. Diagnostics include the newest modules. No effect on the game.

### <a id="adapter-vk_shader_fix"></a>Vulkan shader fixes

Corrects specific shaders that hang the game on the Frame. Comes from a game's recipe.

- `adapter.vk_shader_fix` · revision 2
- **Changes:** Game setting: stored in the build and on the Frame (settings.conf); can be changed without a rebuild.
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Options:**
  - Value: str, default empty.
  - Not in the Game settings dialog (set by a recipe or the CLI).
- **Catalog games (1):** VR4.
- **Source:** [patches/settings.py](../src/frameport/patches/settings.py)

> Vulkan shim (frame.vk_sanitize): SPIR-V modules matching size + SHA-256 get words inserted at a byte offset, for example stores that initialize locals a shader reads before writing (an undefined loop counter hung the GPU in VR4's campaign). Format: &lt;size&gt;:&lt;sha256&gt;:&lt;byte offset&gt;:&lt;word&gt;,&lt;word&gt;,...; several separated by ';'. Comes from a game's recipe.

### <a id="adapter-vk_spec_fixes"></a>Fix depth flicker (Unreal Vulkan)

For Unreal games whose models flicker or show through walls and windows on the Frame (for example Into The Radius 2). Needs a rebuild.

- `adapter.vk_spec_fixes` · revision 2
- **Changes:** Game setting, stored in the build: needs a rebuild.
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Options:**
  - Value: int, default `0`.
  - Game settings → Troubleshooting → "Fix depth flicker (Unreal Vulkan)" (advanced).
- **Catalog games (2):** Into The Radius 2, Metro Awakening.
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `unreal-vulkan-driver-crash` (fatal): The Frame's Vulkan driver crashed on a call from Unreal.
- **Source:** [patches/settings.py](../src/frameport/patches/settings.py)

> Vulkan shim (frame.vk_sanitize): makes two Unreal habits valid Vulkan - depth images get VK_IMAGE_USAGE_TRANSFER_DST_BIT (they are cleared with vkCmdClearDepthStencilImage) and Qualcomm shader-resolve subpasses lose an invalid depth resolve. Found with the validation layer in Into The Radius 2 (flickering models, windows behind models). Also leaves out image barriers without an image and refuses image views without one, which crash the Frame's driver (for example Metro Awakening).

Logs Vulkan mistakes the game makes. Needs a special test build.

- `adapter.vk_validation`
- **Changes:** Game setting: stored in the build and on the Frame (settings.conf); can be changed without a rebuild.
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Options:**
  - Value: int, default `0`.
  - Game settings → Troubleshooting → "Vulkan error checks (log)" (advanced).
- **Source:** [patches/settings.py](../src/frameport/patches/settings.py)

> Diagnostics: the Vulkan shim (frame.vk_sanitize) adds Khronos' validation layer to the game's instance; its findings go to launch.log. The layer library (libVkLayer_khronos_validation.so) must be in the APK.

### <a id="adapter-zink_shader_dump"></a>OpenGL ES shader dump (diagnostics)

Saves the game's shaders to capture one for a fix. No effect on the game.

- `adapter.zink_shader_dump`
- **Changes:** Game setting: stored in the build and on the Frame (settings.conf); can be changed without a rebuild.
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.

### <a id="adapter-zink_shader_fix"></a>OpenGL ES shader fixes

Repairs OpenGL ES shaders that hang the graphics chip, from the game's recipe.

- `adapter.zink_shader_fix`
- **Changes:** Game setting: stored in the build and on the Frame (settings.conf); can be changed without a rebuild.
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Options:**
  - Value: str, default empty.
  - Not in the Game settings dialog (set by a recipe or the CLI).
- **Catalog games (1):** Vader Immortal: Episode I.
- **Source:** [patches/settings.py](../src/frameport/patches/settings.py)

> Shader-fix Vulkan layer (frame.zink_shader_fix) for OpenGL ES games, whose GLSL the Frame's GL driver (Zink) turns into SPIR-V: modules matching size + SHA-256 get words inserted at a byte offset, for example stores that set loop counters and accumulators a shader reads before writing (Vader Immortal's lightspeed jump hung the GPU; found by Klownicle, GitHub #49). Same format as vk_shader_fix. Comes from a game's recipe; the driver's output can change with a Frame update, then the fix no longer matches (logged).

## <a id="group-device"></a>Files and settings on the Frame

Files, environment and window options written on the Frame when a Quest game or Android app is installed. They don't change the APK.

### <a id="device-config_sync"></a>Keep the game's saved resolution in step

Keeps the resolution the game saves in step with the headset's picture size (else the picture is shifted, with black borders, after a sharpness change).

- `device.config_sync`
- **Changes:** Install only: written on the Frame when the game is installed; the APK isn't changed.
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Options:** `files`: text, default none — path relative to files/ -&gt; {setting name: w \| h \| expression}
- **Catalog games (1):** BlazeRush.
- **Source:** [patches/settings.py](../src/frameport/patches/settings.py)

> Some games save their render resolution in a settings file and load it after creating the headset's eye buffers; after a resolution scale change the saved size no longer matches and the picture is displaced or stretched, with black borders (for example BlazeRush's user_config.xml). FramePort writes the values its recipe names into the game's file while the game isn't running (after an install and after a Game settings change), from the Frame's own eye-buffer size times the resolution scale: w and h = the eye buffer's width and height, for example h*16/9. Only existing entries change; the previous file is kept as &lt;file&gt;.frameport-backup. The size is learned from the game's last start, so a file the game wrote before is corrected from the next install or settings change on.

### <a id="device-display_mode"></a>Show as VR or as a flat window

Choose Flat window if a phone or tablet app shows nothing in the headset, VR if a VR app opens as a flat window.

- `device.display_mode` · also for 2D apps
- **Changes:** Install only: written on the Frame when the game is installed; the APK isn't changed.
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Options:** `mode`: str, default empty — vr or flat (empty = automatic)
- **Source:** [patches/settings.py](../src/frameport/patches/settings.py)

> How Lepton runs the app: VR (headless Android, only what the app draws through OpenXR reaches the headset) or a flat window (Lepton's lepton-show-flatscreen marker: the Android window on a screen in the headset, like a phone or tablet app). Automatic uses a flat window for apps without VR code. Choose "Flat window" for a 2D app FramePort took for VR (it shows nothing in the headset), "VR" for a VR app FramePort took for 2D.

### <a id="device-files"></a>Settings files for the game

Puts settings files next to the game on the Frame, for example to turn off an unsupported effect.

- `device.files` · also for 2D apps
- **Changes:** Install only: written on the Frame when the game is installed; the APK isn't changed.
- **Suggested (on):** CryEngine: variable-rate shading isn't supported on the Frame, so user.cfg turns it off (… = 0; The Climb / The Climb 2).
- **Options:** `files`: text, default none — path relative to files/ -&gt; content
- **Catalog games (3):** SUPERHOT VR, The Climb, The Climb 2.
- **Source:** [patches/settings.py](../src/frameport/patches/settings.py)

> Writes config files into the game's Android/data/&lt;package&gt;/files/ on the Frame, to turn off engine features the Frame doesn't support (for example a CryEngine user.cfg with r_variable_rate_shading = 0, as The Climb 2 needs).

### <a id="device-foveation"></a>Foveated rendering (Valve)

Render less detail outside your gaze; adjust the full-resolution area or darken coarse regions to test it.

- `device.foveation` · experimental · revision 3
- **Changes:** Changes the APK (a rebuild and reinstall apply it).
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Options:**
  - `mode`: str, default empty — tracked, fixed or off (empty = Valve's default)
  - `radius`: float, default `0.0`, 0–0.45 — Full-resolution radius; 0 keeps the current runtime default
  - `test`: bool, default `False` — Darken lower-resolution regions (diagnostic)
- **Catalog games (3):** Ocean Rift, Quantum Void, Tea For God.
- **Source:** [patches/settings.py](../src/frameport/patches/settings.py)

> Reduces shading away from the full-resolution area, following each eye's gaze. Default area size keeps the runtime's current profile unchanged. Custom radius is a fraction of the shorter eye-image dimension; the transition ends at twice that radius. Larger areas retain more detail but save less GPU work. Fixed stops the area following your eyes. The optional test darkens actual coarse-shaded fragments; rebuild/reinstall to toggle it. Tested on RE4, Deadpool and Asgard's Wrath 2. The Climb 2 gets a version-guarded private bridge at 1.0 scale; Batman gets its hash-verified allocation fix (unsupported OVRPlugin versions are refused). Other games may need additional fixes; turn this off if artifacts appear.

### <a id="device-hide_navbar"></a>Hide Android's navigation bar

Hides Android's back, home and recents buttons, which cover the app's own buttons.

- `device.hide_navbar` · also for 2D apps
- **Changes:** Install only: written on the Frame when the game is installed; the APK isn't changed.
- **Suggested (on):** 2D app: Android's navigation buttons would cover the app's own controls.
- **Source:** [patches/settings.py](../src/frameport/patches/settings.py)

> Removes Android's back/home/recents buttons from a 2D app's window, where they cover the app's own controls. Turn it off for an app that needs the on-screen back button.

### <a id="device-lepton_env"></a>Extra Lepton settings

Extra settings for the Android container (for testing).

- `device.lepton_env` · also for 2D apps
- **Changes:** Install only: written on the Frame when the game is installed; the APK isn't changed.
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Options:** `env`: text, default none — NAME -&gt; value
- **Catalog games (3):** Into The Radius 2, Metro Awakening, QuestCraft.
- **Source:** [patches/settings.py](../src/frameport/patches/settings.py)

> Environment variables exported by the launcher (for example VK_INSTANCE_LAYERS="" to test without Valve's layers).

### <a id="device-steam_gamepad"></a>Controllers as a gamepad (Steam Input)

Lets the game use your controllers as a gamepad instead of a pointer, for 2D games with touch controls (for example SDL games).

- `device.steam_gamepad` · also for 2D apps
- **Changes:** Install only: written on the Frame when the game is installed; the APK isn't changed.
- **Suggested (on):** 2D app that declares gamepad support (android.hardware.gamepad or Android TV's launcher): pass the controllers to it as a gamepad.
- **Source:** [patches/settings.py](../src/frameport/patches/settings.py)

> Lepton's Android only gets a keyboard, a pointer and touch from the Frame, so a 2D game never sees a controller (the controllers only move the pointer; SDL games show their touch controls). This passes Steam Input's virtual gamepad ("Microsoft X-Box 360 pad", made by Steam for the Frame's controllers and paired Bluetooth pads) into this app's container with an Xbox 360 key layout, and tells SDL games to use it (SDL_GAMECONTROLLER_ALLOW_STEAM_VIRTUAL_GAMEPAD). Steam Input must be on for the game's shortcut; the controllers must be on when the game starts (a pad Steam makes later isn't seen until the next start). The APK isn't changed. Off for one start: FRAMEPORT_NO_GAMEPAD=1 in the game's launch options.

### <a id="device-text_input_window"></a>Show the app's Android window (for typing)

Lets typing reach this app from Steam's on-screen keyboard or your PC's keyboard. VR keeps working.

- `device.text_input_window`
- **Changes:** Install only: written on the Frame when the game is installed; the APK isn't changed.
- **Suggested (on):** App with text fields: key presses only reach a shown Android window.
- **Catalog games (110):** AFFECTED: The Manor, AgeOfJoy, AllInOneSports, Ancient_Dungeon, Arcsmith, Arkio, Assassin's Creed Nexus, Attack on Titan VR: Unbreakable and 102 more.
- **Source:** [patches/settings.py](../src/frameport/patches/settings.py)

> Lepton runs VR apps headless: their Android window is never shown, so it never gets keyboard focus and no key press (Steam's on-screen keyboard, a USB/Bluetooth keyboard, Type on Frame) reaches the app's text fields. With Lepton's lepton-show-flatscreen marker the window is shown (behind the VR view, which keeps working) and Steam's keyboard opens for a selected text field. Steam lists the shown window as "Gamescope" (the Frame's compositor). Pairs with "Make Unity text fields work without a system keyboard".

## <a id="group-pcvr"></a>PC VR (Proton and Revive)

Options for PC VR games, which run through Proton on the Frame (or Revive on this PC).

### <a id="pcvr-launch_args"></a>Launch options (SteamVR or OpenXR)

Starts the game with options, for example to choose SteamVR or OpenXR.

- `pcvr.launch_args`
- **Changes:** Applied when the PC VR game is installed or started; no rebuild.
- **Suggested (on):** Selects SteamVR/OpenXR (…).
- **Options:** `args`: str, default empty — arguments, for example -hmd=OpenXR
- **Catalog games (2):** Eleven: Table Tennis VR (PC VR), SUPERHOT VR (PC VR).
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `unity-vr-init` (error): The game's Unity log shows that a VR device failed to start.
- **Source:** [patches/pcvr.py](../src/frameport/patches/pcvr.py)

> Command-line arguments for the game program. Games that support several VR runtimes pick one with an argument, for example Unreal's -hmd=OpenXR or -hmd=SteamVR, Unity's -vrmode OpenVR, or a game's own switch (-Runtime=OpenXRHMD). FramePort fills them in from the game files (the repack's VD.bat with the Oculus module swapped for OpenXR, else the engine's usual switch).

### <a id="pcvr-libovr_redirect"></a>Provide the Oculus runtime from Revive (Frame)

Points Oculus games at Revive on the Frame.

- `pcvr.libovr_redirect`
- **Changes:** Applied when the PC VR game is installed or started; no rebuild.
- **Offered (off):** Supports SteamVR/OpenXR itself: no Oculus runtime needed.
- **Suggested (on):** Lets the game find Revive's runtime on the Frame (doesn't bypass its signature check).
- **Source:** [patches/pcvr.py](../src/frameport/patches/pcvr.py)

> On the Frame, place Revive's runtime (FramePort's Revive, or the repack's bundled LibRevive) where the game's Oculus SDK looks for LibOVRRT so it can load a VR runtime (pure runtime substitution — what Revive's LoadLibrary hook does on Windows; that hook doesn't work under Proton on the Frame). It does NOT bypass the Oculus runtime signature check: a game that verifies the runtime's signature will still refuse it. Ignored on this PC (Revive's hook handles it there).

### <a id="pcvr-no_crash_reporter"></a>No Unreal crash reporter

Stops Unreal's crash reporter, which can block the game from starting.

- `pcvr.no_crash_reporter`
- **Changes:** Applied when the PC VR game is installed or started; no rebuild.
- **Suggested (on):** Unreal game: close on a crash instead of showing the crash reporter.
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `unreal-crash` (fatal): The game crashed (Unreal's crash reporter started).
- **Source:** [patches/pcvr.py](../src/frameport/patches/pcvr.py)

> Unreal games start CrashReportClient when they crash, which leaves a crash dialog instead of simply closing. This passes -nocrashreports to the game and, on the Frame, renames the game's copy of CrashReportClient.exe so it can't start (your game files on this PC aren't changed).

### <a id="pcvr-oculus_unreal"></a>Patch Oculus detection for Unreal (Frame)

Lets Unreal games accept a headset that isn't an Oculus Rift.

- `pcvr.oculus_unreal`
- **Changes:** Applied when the PC VR game is installed or started; no rebuild.
- **Offered (off):** Uses SteamVR/OpenXR, not its Oculus plugin.
- **Suggested (on):** Unreal game: its Oculus plugin checks for the Oculus service before it starts VR.
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `oculus-hmd-event` (error): The game runs as a flat window because FramePort's Oculus detection helper failed.
- **Source:** [patches/pcvr.py](../src/frameport/patches/pcvr.py)

> The PC VR counterpart of OVRPort's 'Patch Oculus detection for Unreal'. Unreal's Oculus plugin only starts when the Oculus service announces a headset (the Windows event 'OculusHMDConnected'); without it the game runs as a flat window. On the Frame the launcher runs the game through FramePort's small helper (fp_oculushmd.exe) that provides that event while the game runs, instead of relying only on Revive's hook of the check. Ignored on this PC (the Oculus app or Revive handle it there).

### <a id="pcvr-proton_env"></a>Extra Proton settings (Frame)

Extra settings for Proton (for testing).

- `pcvr.proton_env`
- **Changes:** Applied when the PC VR game is installed or started; no rebuild.
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Options:** `env`: text, default empty — KEY=value lines
- **Source:** [patches/pcvr.py](../src/frameport/patches/pcvr.py)

> Environment variables for the Proton launcher on the Frame (for example DXVK_HUD=fps), one KEY=value per line.

### <a id="pcvr-proton_log"></a>Proton debug log (Frame)

Writes a detailed Proton log for troubleshooting.

- `pcvr.proton_log`
- **Changes:** Applied when the PC VR game is installed or started; no rebuild.
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `dxvk-device-lost` (fatal): The GPU stopped responding while running the game (D3D through DXVK on freedreno).
  - `oculus-hmd-event` (error): The game runs as a flat window because FramePort's Oculus detection helper failed.
  - `unity-crash` (fatal): The game crashed (Unity's crash handler wrote a report; the Unity log in the launch log shows the stack).
  - `unreal-crash` (fatal): The game crashed (Unreal's crash reporter started).
  - `wine-crash` (error): The game crashed under Wine/Proton.
- **Source:** [patches/pcvr.py](../src/frameport/patches/pcvr.py)

> Write Proton's log (PROTON_LOG=1) to steam-&lt;appid&gt;.log in the game folder on the Frame. Slower; use while debugging a game that doesn't start.

### <a id="pcvr-proton_tool"></a>Proton version (Frame)

Which Proton runs the game on the Frame. Stable is smoother; try Experimental if the game doesn't start or runs badly.

- `pcvr.proton_tool`
- **Changes:** Applied when the PC VR game is installed or started; no rebuild.
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Options:** `tool`: str, default empty — proton-stable (default), proton-experimental, or a compat tool name
- **Source:** [patches/pcvr.py](../src/frameport/patches/pcvr.py)

> Which Proton build runs the game on the Frame: the stable Proton (the default: smoother in our tests) or Proton Experimental (gets Valve's ARM64 fixes first; try it when a game doesn't start or runs badly). Also takes any compat tool name from the Frame's ARM64 list.

### <a id="pcvr-repack_launcher"></a>Use the repack's launcher (bundled Revive)

Starts the game with the launcher that came with your copy.

- `pcvr.repack_launcher`
- **Changes:** Applied when the PC VR game is installed or started; no rebuild.
- **Suggested (on):** The game folder has its own Revive and loader (…): run the game directly.
- **Conflicts with:** [`pcvr.revive`](#pcvr-revive)
- **Options:** `dlls`: str, default empty — loader DLLs next to the exe (comma-separated)
- **Source:** [patches/pcvr.py](../src/frameport/patches/pcvr.py)

> Some game folders are already set up for SteamVR: a Revive copy (LibRevive64.dll) next to the game, started by a small loader DLL (for example xinput1_3.dll) that Windows loads from the game's folder. Then FramePort starts the game program directly — like double-clicking it — instead of through its own Revive (two Revives conflict; for example the Oculus Platform check then fails). On the Frame, Wine is told to use those loader DLLs from the game folder instead of its own.

### <a id="pcvr-revive"></a>Revive (Oculus LibOVR → OpenXR)

Lets games made for Oculus PCs run on SteamVR.

- `pcvr.revive`
- **Changes:** Applied when the PC VR game is installed or started; no rebuild.
- **Offered (off):** The game folder already has its own Revive set up (see 'Use the repack's launcher'); a second Revive breaks it.
- **Offered (off):** Supports SteamVR/OpenXR itself: SteamVR / the Frame run it directly.
- **Suggested (on):** Oculus/LibOVR game: Revive translates it to SteamVR/OpenXR (without it it runs flat).
- **Conflicts with:** [`pcvr.repack_launcher`](#pcvr-repack_launcher)
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `unreal-crash` (fatal): The game crashed (Unreal's crash reporter started).
- **Source:** [patches/pcvr.py](../src/frameport/patches/pcvr.py)

> Launch the game through Revive's injector, which translates the Oculus PC SDK (LibOVR) to OpenXR. Needed by every Oculus Rift game that isn't OpenXR-native. FramePort downloads Revive itself.

### <a id="pcvr-revive_openvr"></a>Revive: SteamVR (OpenVR) backend on PC

On this PC, runs Revive through SteamVR (works with more headsets).

- `pcvr.revive_openvr`
- **Changes:** Applied when the PC VR game is installed or started; no rebuild.
- **Offered (off):** Not launched through FramePort's Revive.
- **Suggested (on):** PC: Revive's SteamVR/OpenVR backend is the most reliable path.
- **Requires:** [`pcvr.revive`](#pcvr-revive)
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `openxr-missing-ext` (fatal): The VR runtime lacks a feature Revive needs (XR_KHR_D3D11_enable or win32 time conversion).
- **Source:** [patches/pcvr.py](../src/frameport/patches/pcvr.py)

> On this PC, launch the game through Revive's OpenVR backend, which talks straight to SteamVR — the original, most reliable Revive path. On by default for PC installs. Turn it off to use Revive's newer OpenXR backend instead. Ignored on the Frame (which always uses OpenXR).

### <a id="pcvr-steamvr_tuning"></a>Automatic SteamVR performance settings (this PC)

Picks a refresh rate and motion smoothing that suit the game on this PC.

- `pcvr.steamvr_tuning`
- **Changes:** Applied when the PC VR game is installed or started; no rebuild.
- **Suggested (on):** Adjusts the refresh rate / motion smoothing when the game can't keep up.
- **Options:**
  - `refresh`: float, default `0.0`, 0–144 — refresh rate in Hz (0 = automatic)
  - `smoothing`: str, default `auto` — motion smoothing: auto, on, off, always or global
- **Catalog games (4):** Beat Saber (PC VR), Eleven: Table Tennis VR (PC VR), Pistol Whip (PC VR), SUPERHOT VR (PC VR).
- **Source:** [patches/pcvr.py](../src/frameport/patches/pcvr.py)

> Before each Play on this PC, FramePort reads SteamVR's record of the game's last session (frames dropped; frame times from fpsVR if installed). If it dropped frames, it lowers the game's refresh rate to one whose frame budget fits (for example 96 → 90 Hz) and turns motion smoothing on, through SteamVR's per-application settings; each later session can step down again. Set a refresh rate or smoothing mode here to choose yourself. Ignored on the Frame.

### <a id="pcvr-vr_overlay"></a>SteamVR overlay app (Frame)

Lets SteamVR on the Frame show this overlay app over your games (and start it with SteamVR).

- `pcvr.vr_overlay`
- **Changes:** Applied when the PC VR game is installed or started; no rebuild.
- **Suggested:** not automatically; set on the game page (Customize), by a recipe or after a launch test.
- **Options:** `autostart`: bool, default `True` — start with SteamVR
- **Source:** [patches/pcvr.py](../src/frameport/patches/pcvr.py)

> For overlay apps (fpsVR, wrist watches and other SteamVR add-ons that draw over games instead of being a game): FramePort registers the app with the Frame's SteamVR, which draws its overlays over whatever you play there, Quest and PC VR games alike. With 'start with SteamVR' on, SteamVR starts it by itself (also after a restart); otherwise start it from the library. It isn't launch-tested (it shows nothing without a game). Ignored on this PC.

### <a id="pcvr-xr_timefix"></a>Frame OpenXR compatibility layer

Lets games written for newer OpenXR versions run on the Frame.

- `pcvr.xr_timefix`
- **Changes:** Applied when the PC VR game is installed or started; no rebuild.
- **Suggested (on):** The Frame's OpenXR runtime rejects Proton's OpenXR 1.1 request without it.
- **Catalog games (5):** Beat Saber (PC VR), Eleven: Table Tennis VR (PC VR), Pistol Whip (PC VR), Rick and Morty: Virtual Rick-ality (PC VR), SUPERHOT VR (PC VR).
- **Suggested by launch-test signatures:**
  - `openxr-api-version` (fatal): The game got no VR, so it runs as a flat window or Revive fails.
  - `openxr-missing-ext` (fatal): The VR runtime lacks a feature Revive needs (XR_KHR_D3D11_enable or win32 time conversion).
  - `openxr-time-conversion` (error): The VR runtime refused a time conversion that Proton needs for Windows games' performance-counter times.
- **Source:** [patches/pcvr.py](../src/frameport/patches/pcvr.py)

> Loads FramePort's OpenXR layer under Proton on the Frame. The Frame's SteamVR runtime only accepts OpenXR 1.0 apps, but Proton's VR helper asks for 1.1, so without the layer VR never starts (the game shows as a flat window, or Revive fails with 'Unable to load LibOVRRT DLL'); the layer retries as 1.0. It also emulates xrConvertTimespecTimeToTimeKHR if a runtime refuses it. Ignored on this PC.
